## Søren Kierkegaard Quotes with Verified Sources (8)

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/quote-source/soren-kierkegaard

Quote sources

# Søren Kierkegaard quote sources

8 passages attributed to Søren Kierkegaard in this archive, each with the locator that lets you find it in the work itself — and the one thing that most often goes wrong when people quote Kierkegaard.

[Quote source](https://www.philosophydef.com/quote-source) / Søren Kierkegaard

How to cite this author, and what circulates under the name that is not theirs to give.

## Sourcing profile

Language of the works

Danish

Cited here from

The Sickness unto Death, The Concept of Anxiety, Either/Or, and the Journals (1843).

How to cite it

Name the pseudonym as well as Kierkegaard. The Sickness unto Death is signed by Anti-Climacus, The Concept of Anxiety by Vigilius Haufniensis, and Either/Or by two more, because the pseudonymity is part of the work rather than a pen name.

Where quotations of this author go wrong

Kierkegaard published his philosophical books under pseudonyms whose positions he did not simply hold, and he said so explicitly in “A First and Last Explanation,” which he signed with his own name. Quoting one of the pseudonyms as Kierkegaard's opinion is exactly the reading he wrote the explanation to prevent. The Journals are a separate corpus with their own numbering and dates.

## Wang Yangming Quotes with Verified Sources (9)

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/quote-source/wang-yangming

Quote sources

# Wang Yangming quote sources

9 passages attributed to Wang Yangming in this archive, each with the locator that lets you find it in the work itself — and the one thing that most often goes wrong when people quote Yangming.

[Quote source](https://www.philosophydef.com/quote-source) / Wang Yangming

How to cite this author, and what circulates under the name that is not theirs to give.

## Sourcing profile

Language of the works

Classical Chinese

Cited here from

Instructions for Practical Living (Chuanxilu), by juan and entry, plus one entry recorded as traditional last words.

How to cite it

Juan (volume) and entry number. The Chuanxilu is a record of conversations and letters compiled by disciples, and the numbering is what identifies an entry.

Where quotations of this author go wrong

The famous deathbed saying attributed to him is not in the Chuanxilu; it is a traditional attribution recorded by later followers, and this archive files it as such. Wang also used 知行合一 (“the unity of knowledge and action”) as a technical term against Zhu Xi's teaching, so the phrase does not mean what “knowledge and action go together” suggests to a modern reader.

The register

## Zhuangzi Quotes with Verified Sources (10)

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/quote-source/zhuangzi

Quote sources

# Zhuangzi quote sources

10 passages attributed to Zhuangzi in this archive, each with the locator that lets you find it in the work itself — and the one thing that most often goes wrong when people quote Zhuangzi.

[Quote source](https://www.philosophydef.com/quote-source) / Zhuangzi

How to cite this author, and what circulates under the name that is not theirs to give.

## Sourcing profile

Language of the works

Classical Chinese

Cited here from

The Zhuangzi — the Inner Chapters (Free and Easy Wandering, Discussion on Making All Things Equal, The Primacy of Nourishing Life, The Great Ancestral Teacher) and chapters from the Outer and Miscellaneous books.

How to cite it

Give the Chinese chapter number as well as the translated title. Chapter names vary wildly between translators — the same book is “Qiwulun,” “Discussion on Making All Things Equal,” and “On the Equality of Things” — so the number is the only stable identifier.

Where quotations of this author go wrong

The received text has thirty-three chapters in Guo Xiang's fourth-century recension, and only the first seven, the Inner Chapters, have a strong claim to a single hand. Quoting from the Outer Chapters as the words of Zhuangzi assigns to one person material that most scholars treat as later work in his tradition.

## Africana Philosophy Quotes

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/schools/africana-philosophy

School

# Africana Philosophy quotes

Africana philosophy names philosophical work from Africa and the African diaspora—written critique, conceptual analysis, and political thought—rather than a single folk worldview.

52 passages · 9 voices in this archive selection

## Overview

Modern debates distinguish ethnophilosophy from professional philosophy (Hountondji), pursue conceptual decolonization (Wiredu), reclaim agency under colonialism (Fanon, Césaire), and articulate cosmopolitan ethics (Appiah). Ubuntu-related work (e.g. Ramose) treats communal personhood carefully as philosophy, not slogan.

## Historical notes

Early modern figures such as Anton Wilhelm Amo sit beside twentieth-century Négritude and postcolonial critique. The archive’s Africana passages emphasize verifiable texts over invented ancient Egyptian ‘quotations.’

## Core ideas

-   African philosophy exists as literature and argument, not only as collective myth.
-   Conceptual decolonization asks which categories travel and which distort.
-   Colonialism damages both the colonized and the colonizer’s humanity.
-   Personhood and community (Ubuntu debates) repay careful philosophical treatment.

## Thinkers in this archive

[Sophie Oluwole](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/sophie-oluwole) , [Kwasi Wiredu](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/kwasi-wiredu) , [Paulin Hountondji](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/paulin-hountondji) , [Frantz Fanon](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/frantz-fanon) , [Léopold Sédar Senghor](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/leopold-sedar-senghor) , [Kwame Anthony Appiah](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/kwame-anthony-appiah) , [Aimé Césaire](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/aime-cesaire) , [Anton Wilhelm Amo](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/anton-wilhelm-amo) , [Mogobe B. Ramose](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/mogobe-b-ramose)

## FAQ

### What is Africana philosophy?

It is philosophy produced in African and diaspora contexts—texts, arguments, and concepts—across ethics, politics, language, and method.

### Who are major Africana philosophers in this archive?

Kwasi Wiredu, Paulin Hountondji, Frantz Fanon, Aimé Césaire, Kwame Anthony Appiah, Léopold Sédar Senghor, Anton Wilhelm Amo, and Mogobe B. Ramose, among others.

## Analytic Philosophy Quotes

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/schools/analytic-philosophy

School

# Analytic Philosophy quotes

Analytic philosophy emphasizes argumentative clarity, logical analysis, and careful attention to language—without reducing to a single doctrine.

28 passages · 4 voices in this archive selection

## Overview

From early logic and ordinary-language debates to ethics of intention and virtue (Anscombe, Foot) and philosophy of language (Wittgenstein), analytic work in this archive favors precise distinctions over rhetorical flourish.

## Historical notes

Twentieth-century analytic philosophy grows from Frege, Russell, Moore, and the Vienna Circle into postwar Oxford and contemporary ethics, mind, and language.

## Core ideas

-   Clarify concepts before building systems.
-   Language and logic shape what can be said truly.
-   Moral philosophy can be rigorous without ignoring practice.
-   Intention and action repay careful description.

## Thinkers in this archive

[Ludwig Wittgenstein](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/ludwig-wittgenstein) , [Bertrand Russell](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/bertrand-russell) , [Elizabeth Anscombe](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/elizabeth-anscombe) , [Philippa Foot](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/philippa-foot)

## FAQ

### What is analytic philosophy?

It is a family of approaches valuing clarity, argument, and analysis of language and concepts—especially in the English-speaking tradition.

### Is analytic philosophy only about language?

No. Language is a method and topic, but analytic work also covers mind, ethics, metaphysics, and science.

## Confucian Quotes & Confucianism

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/schools/confucianism

School

# Confucianism quotes

Confucianism is a family of ethical and political teachings centered on humaneness, ritual propriety, learning, and the cultivation of character in relationships.

73 passages · 13 voices in this archive selection

## Overview

From Confucius and Mencius to Xunzi and later Neo-Confucians such as Zhu Xi and Wang Yangming, the tradition debates human nature, education, and rightful government while sharing a concern for moral formation through practice.

## Historical notes

Classical Confucianism emerges in the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods; imperial China institutionalized Confucian learning; modern New Confucians reinterpret the tradition for contemporary societies.

## Core ideas

-   Ren (humaneness) and li (ritual) shape ethical life.
-   Learning and self-cultivation are lifelong.
-   Family and political roles are moral arenas.
-   Debate continues on whether nature is good (Mencius) or needs shaping (Xunzi).

## Thinkers in this archive

[Confucius](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/confucius) , [Zengzi](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/zengzi) , [Mencius](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/mencius) , [Xunzi](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/xunzi) , [The Great Learning](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/the-great-learning) , [The Doctrine of the Mean](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/the-doctrine-of-the-mean) , [The Book of Changes](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/the-book-of-changes) , [Zhang Zai](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/zhang-zai) , [Zhu Xi](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/zhu-xi) , [Wang Yangming](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/wang-yangming) , [Feng Youlan](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/feng-youlan) , [Liang Shuming](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/liang-shuming) , [Wang Fuzhi](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/wang-fuzhi)

## FAQ

### What is Confucianism?

It is a tradition of ethical and political thought emphasizing humaneness, ritual, education, and cultivated character.

### Who are key Confucian thinkers?

Confucius, Mencius, and Xunzi are classical pillars; Zhu Xi and Wang Yangming are major Neo-Confucians.

## Daoist Quotes & Daoism

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/schools/daoism

School

# Daoism quotes

Daoism (Taoism) names philosophical and religious currents oriented to the Dao—the Way—often emphasizing naturalness, transformation, and non-coercive action.

21 passages · 2 voices in this archive selection

## Overview

The Daodejing and Zhuangzi are foundational philosophical texts. Themes include wuwei (non-forcing action), critique of rigid naming, soft power, and perspectival freedom. Religious Daoism develops parallel practices; this page focuses on philosophical quotations in the archive.

## Historical notes

Classical Daoist texts take shape in the Warring States period; later commentary and religious movements expand the tradition across East Asia and into global translation.

## Core ideas

-   Align with the Dao rather than forcing outcomes.
-   Softness and flexibility can overcome rigidity.
-   Fixed distinctions and names can distort living reality.
-   Skillful spontaneity emerges from practiced attunement.

## Thinkers in this archive

[Laozi](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/laozi) , [Zhuangzi](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/zhuangzi)

## FAQ

### What is Daoism?

It is a family of Chinese traditions centered on the Dao, naturalness, and often wuwei—acting without forcing.

### Who are the main Daoist philosophers?

Laozi and Zhuangzi are the most-read philosophical figures in English, though the textual history is complex.

## Empiricism in Philosophy

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/schools/empiricism

School

# Empiricism quotes

Empiricism treats experience as the primary source of ideas and the test of knowledge claims about the world.

22 passages · 4 voices in this archive selection

## Overview

British empiricists such as Locke, Berkeley, and Hume analyze how sensation and reflection generate ideas, and how far certainty extends. Empiricism shapes philosophy of science and everyday standards of evidence.

## Historical notes

Early modern empiricism debates innate ideas and causation; later logical empiricism and contemporary naturalistic epistemology continue the lineage in new forms.

## Core ideas

-   Ideas derive from experience.
-   Claims about the world require empirical credentials.
-   Skepticism about metaphysics beyond experience is a standing option.
-   Science exemplifies disciplined experiential inquiry.

## Thinkers in this archive

[Francis Bacon](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/francis-bacon) , [John Locke](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/john-locke) , [George Berkeley](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/george-berkeley) , [David Hume](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/david-hume)

## FAQ

### What is empiricism?

It is the view that experience is the primary source of knowledge about the world.

### Who are the main empiricists?

Locke, Berkeley, and Hume are the classic early modern figures.

### Where can I read empiricism quotes?

## Existentialism Quotes | Sartre, Camus & Kierkegaard

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/schools/existentialism

School

# Existentialism quotes

Existentialism names a family of philosophies that treat human existence, freedom, and responsibility as primary—often before abstract systems.

53 passages · 10 voices in this archive selection

## Overview

Though diverse, existential writers share concerns with anxiety, authenticity, bad faith, absurdity, and the demand to choose under uncertainty. Kierkegaard and Nietzsche prepare the ground; Sartre, Beauvoir, and Camus make mid-century public debates about freedom and meaning.

## Historical notes

Nineteenth-century precursors meet twentieth-century phenomenology and postwar literature. Not all associated figures accepted the label—Camus resisted “existentialist”—yet the cluster remains useful for readers of freedom and meaning.

## Core ideas

-   Existence precedes essence for human beings (Sartre’s slogan).
-   Freedom brings responsibility; evasion is bad faith.
-   Meaning may be created, discovered, or confronted as absurd.
-   Concrete situations matter more than empty abstractions.

## Thinkers in this archive

[Blaise Pascal](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/blaise-pascal) , [Søren Kierkegaard](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/soren-kierkegaard) , [Jean-Paul Sartre](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/jean-paul-sartre) , [Albert Camus](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/albert-camus) , [Simone de Beauvoir](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/simone-de-beauvoir) , [Simone Weil](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/simone-weil) , [José Ortega y Gasset](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/jose-ortega-y-gasset) , [Karl Jaspers](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/karl-jaspers) , [Paul Tillich](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/paul-tillich) , [Gabriel Marcel](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/gabriel-marcel)

## FAQ

### What is existentialism?

It is a philosophical approach emphasizing concrete human existence, freedom, choice, and responsibility.

### Is Camus an existentialist?

Camus is often grouped with existential writers but preferred the language of the absurd and revolt; read him alongside, not simply under, Sartre.

## German Idealism Quotes

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/schools/german-idealism

School

# German Idealism quotes

German Idealism develops post-Kantian systems in which freedom, self-consciousness, and historical reason are tightly linked.

15 passages · 4 voices in this archive selection

## Overview

After Kant’s critical turn, Fichte, Schelling, and Hegel (and related receptions) argue about the absolute, dialectic, and ethical life. Passages here emphasize freedom realized in thought and institutions.

## Historical notes

Late eighteenth- and early nineteenth-century German philosophy sets agendas for Marxism, existentialism, pragmatism, and contemporary continental thought.

## Core ideas

-   Freedom is not only private choice but realized form.
-   Self-consciousness develops through relation and recognition.
-   System and history can be thought together.
-   Critique of knowledge opens metaphysics rather than ending it.

## Thinkers in this archive

[G. W. F. Hegel](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/g-w-f-hegel) , [Immanuel Kant](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/immanuel-kant) , [Johann Wolfgang von Goethe](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/johann-wolfgang-von-goethe) , [Friedrich Schiller](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/friedrich-schiller)

## FAQ

### What is German Idealism?

It is the post-Kantian movement treating mind, freedom, and reality as systematically interrelated—often via dialectic.

### Is Kant a German Idealist?

Kant is the decisive precursor; ‘German Idealism’ usually names the generation that radicalized his insights.

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/schools

Enter through a tradition, then follow thinkers and themes.

## [Stoicism](https://www.philosophydef.com/schools/stoicism)

Virtue, nature, and the discipline of judgment.

Seneca · Epictetus · Marcus

## [Existentialism](https://www.philosophydef.com/schools/existentialism)

Freedom, responsibility, absurdity, and authentic choice.

Sartre · Beauvoir · Camus

## [Confucianism](https://www.philosophydef.com/schools/confucianism)

Humaneness, ritual, learning, and cultivated roles.

Confucius · Mencius · Xunzi

## [Daoism](https://www.philosophydef.com/schools/daoism)

The Dao, wuwei, and naturalness without forced order.

Laozi · Zhuangzi

## [Rationalism](https://www.philosophydef.com/schools/rationalism)

Reason, a priori insight, and systematic metaphysics.

Descartes · Spinoza · Leibniz

## [Empiricism](https://www.philosophydef.com/schools/empiricism)

Experience as the primary source of ideas and evidence.

Locke · Berkeley · Hume

## [Pragmatism](https://www.philosophydef.com/schools/pragmatism)

Meaning, truth, and inquiry tied to practical consequences.

Peirce · James · Dewey

## [Africana Philosophy](https://www.philosophydef.com/schools/africana-philosophy)

Critique, conceptual decolonization, and diaspora thought.

Wiredu · Hountondji · Fanon · Appiah

## [Islamic Philosophy](https://www.philosophydef.com/schools/islamic-philosophy)

Falsafa: intellect, prophecy, and demonstrative science.

Avicenna · Averroes · al-Farabi

## [Analytic Philosophy](https://www.philosophydef.com/schools/analytic-philosophy)

Clarity, logic, language, intention, and mind.

Wittgenstein · Anscombe · Foot

## [Neo-Confucianism](https://www.philosophydef.com/schools/neo-confucianism)

Principle, heart-mind, and the unity of knowledge and action.

Zhu Xi · Wang Yangming

## [Platonism](https://www.philosophydef.com/schools/platonism)

Forms, the Good, and dialectic as education of desire.

Plato · later Platonic lineages

## [Kyoto School](https://www.philosophydef.com/schools/kyoto-school)

Absolute nothingness, experience, and religious worldview.

Nishida · Nishitani

## [German Idealism](https://www.philosophydef.com/schools/german-idealism)

Freedom, spirit, and systematic post-Kantian reason.

Hegel · related idealists

## [Jewish Rationalism](https://www.philosophydef.com/schools/jewish-rationalism)

Reason, revelation, law, and negative theology.

Maimonides · Saadia Gaon

## Islamic Philosophy Quotes

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/schools/islamic-philosophy

School

# Islamic Philosophy quotes

Islamic philosophy names the classical falsafa tradition and related theological-philosophical debate across the Islamic world.

36 passages · 6 voices in this archive selection

## Overview

Figures such as al-Farabi, Avicenna (Ibn Sina), Averroes (Ibn Rushd), and al-Ghazali debate intellect, prophecy, causation, and the relation of philosophy to revelation. The archive gathers English renderings with honest confidence marks when Arabic originals are not transcribed.

## Historical notes

From the translation movement through Andalusian Aristotelianism and later critiques, Islamic philosophy shaped Jewish and Latin scholastic thought as well as its own lineages.

## Core ideas

-   Philosophy and prophecy can be ordered without collapsing into each other.
-   Metaphysics of being and intellect remains central (especially Avicenna).
-   Demonstrative science has norms that rhetoric and dialectic do not replace.
-   Critique of the philosophers is itself a philosophical act (al-Ghazali and responses).

## Thinkers in this archive

[Al-Ghazali](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/al-ghazali) , [Ibn Khaldun](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/ibn-khaldun) , [Averroes](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/averroes) , [Al-Farabi](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/al-farabi) , [Avicenna](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/avicenna) , [Ibn Tufayl](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/ibn-tufayl)

## FAQ

### What is Islamic philosophy?

It is the philosophical tradition developed in Islamic civilizations, often engaging Greek sources alongside Qur’anic and legal discourse.

### Who are key Islamic philosophers?

Common entry points include al-Farabi, Avicenna, Averroes, al-Ghazali, Ibn Tufayl, and Ibn Khaldun.

## Jewish Rationalism Quotes

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/schools/jewish-rationalism

School

# Jewish Rationalism quotes

Jewish rationalism seeks coherence between philosophical reason and Jewish revelation, law, and prophecy.

14 passages · 3 voices in this archive selection

## Overview

Saadia, Maimonides, and related figures argue about divine attributes, creation, prophecy, and ethical law. This hub collects English passages under the archive’s Jewish Rationalism label.

## Historical notes

Medieval Jewish philosophy develops in Islamic and later European contexts, shaping both Jewish thought and Latin scholastic debates.

## Core ideas

-   Reason can clarify without dissolving revelation.
-   Negative theology guards speech about God.
-   Law and intellect jointly form the human good.
-   Prophecy has epistemic and political dimensions.

## Thinkers in this archive

[Maimonides](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/maimonides) , [Saadia Gaon](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/saadia-gaon) , [Judah Halevi](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/judah-halevi)

## FAQ

### What is Jewish rationalism?

It is a tradition of Jewish philosophy that integrates rigorous reasoning with scripture, law, and communal practice.

### Who are key Jewish rationalist philosophers?

Saadia Gaon and Maimonides are central entry points in this archive; related figures appear under adjacent labels.

## Kyoto School Quotes

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/schools/kyoto-school

School

# Kyoto School quotes

The Kyoto School brings Zen and Mahayana insights into dialogue with Western philosophy, especially around nothingness, experience, and the religious worldview.

16 passages · 3 voices in this archive selection

## Overview

Nishida’s logic of place and contradictory self-identity, Nishitani’s religion and nothingness, and related figures (including Watsuji’s ethics of betweenness in adjacent debates) shape this hub’s English passages.

## Historical notes

Emerging around Kyoto University in the early twentieth century, the school remains central to comparative philosophy of religion and modern Japanese thought.

## Core ideas

-   Absolute nothingness is not mere negation.
-   Self and world co-determine in the place (basho) of experience.
-   Religion discloses a logic ordinary objectivity misses.
-   Emptiness (śūnyatā) can be philosophically articulated without slogans.

## Thinkers in this archive

[Nishida Kitaro](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/nishida-kitaro) , [Nishitani Keiji](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/nishitani-keiji) , [Watsuji Tetsuro](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/watsuji-tetsuro)

## FAQ

### What is the Kyoto School?

It is a modern Japanese philosophical movement engaging Western philosophy with Mahayana and Zen concepts, especially nothingness and experience.

### Who are major Kyoto School thinkers?

Nishida Kitaro and Nishitani Keiji are central; related figures appear alongside them in comparative ethics and religion.

### Where can I find Kyoto School quotes?

This school page gathers verified English renderings from the archive’s Kyoto School label.

## Neo-Confucianism Quotes

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/schools/neo-confucianism

School

# Neo-Confucianism quotes

Neo-Confucianism renews Confucian ethics through metaphysics of principle and heart-mind, shaping East Asian education and moral practice.

20 passages · 4 voices in this archive selection

## Overview

Zhu Xi systematizes li and qi; Wang Yangming emphasizes the unity of knowledge and action and innate moral knowing. The archive’s passages stress cultivation, sincerity, and practical learning.

## Historical notes

Song–Ming Neo-Confucianism responds to Buddhist and Daoist challenges while reclaiming Confucian classics as living moral psychology.

## Core ideas

-   Principle (li) structures both cosmos and ethics.
-   Self-cultivation is intellectual and practical.
-   Knowledge and action should not be split (Wang Yangming).
-   Sincerity and investigation of things form a paired discipline.

## Thinkers in this archive

[Zhang Zai](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/zhang-zai) , [Zhu Xi](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/zhu-xi) , [Wang Yangming](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/wang-yangming) , [Wang Fuzhi](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/wang-fuzhi)

## FAQ

### What is Neo-Confucianism?

It is the Song–Ming renewal of Confucian thought with a richer metaphysics and a focus on moral self-cultivation.

### How does it differ from classical Confucianism?

It keeps humaneness and ritual central while developing systematic accounts of principle, heart-mind, and practice.

## Platonism Quotes & Platonic Philosophy

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/schools/platonism

School

# Platonism quotes

Platonism treats intelligible forms—especially the Good—as more real than shifting appearances, and education as an ascent of the soul.

30 passages · 7 voices in this archive selection

## Overview

Plato’s dialogues and later Platonic schools explore justice, love, knowledge, and political order through dialectic. This archive page gathers English passages tagged to Platonic lineages.

## Historical notes

From the Academy through Middle and Neoplatonism into Renaissance and modern revivals, Platonism remains a standing option in metaphysics and ethics.

## Core ideas

-   Forms explain sameness amid change.
-   The Good orients knowledge and politics.
-   Dialectic educates desire as well as intellect.
-   Love can be a ladder from particular beauty to the Beautiful.

## Thinkers in this archive

[Plato](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/plato) , [Plutarch](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/plutarch) , [Boethius](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/boethius) , [Plotinus](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/plotinus) , [Iris Murdoch](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/iris-murdoch) , [Damascius](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/damascius) , [Synesius of Cyrene](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/synesius-of-cyrene)

## FAQ

### What is Platonism?

It is the family of views descending from Plato that privilege intelligible reality, dialectic, and the ethical centrality of the good.

### Is Platonism only Plato?

No. Later Platonists develop the tradition; this page includes related Platonic school labels in the archive.

## Pragmatism Quotes & Philosophy

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/schools/pragmatism

School

# Pragmatism quotes

Pragmatism treats meaning and truth in relation to practical consequences and the self-correcting practice of inquiry.

17 passages · 4 voices in this archive selection

## Overview

Peirce, James, and Dewey developed overlapping but distinct pragmatisms: clarification of concepts by conceivable effects, truth as workable belief under inquiry, and democracy as experimental associated living.

## Historical notes

Classical American pragmatism emerges in the late nineteenth century and influences education, law, religion, and contemporary neo-pragmatism.

## Core ideas

-   Clarify ideas by their practical bearings.
-   Inquiry aims at truth as the ideal end of investigation.
-   Experience is experimental and revisable.
-   Democracy and education are laboratories of growth.

## Thinkers in this archive

[William James](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/william-james) , [John Dewey](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/john-dewey) , [Hu Shi](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/hu-shi) , [Charles Sanders Peirce](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/charles-sanders-peirce)

## FAQ

### What is pragmatism in philosophy?

It is a family of views linking meaning, truth, and knowledge to practical consequences and inquiry.

### Who founded pragmatism?

Charles Sanders Peirce coined key formulations; William James and John Dewey developed highly influential versions.

### Where are pragmatism quotes?

See the English passages below and thinker pages for Peirce, James, and Dewey.

## Rationalism in Philosophy

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/schools/rationalism

School

# Rationalism quotes

Rationalism holds that reason plays a primary role in knowledge—often defending a priori insight against pure empiricism.

36 passages · 7 voices in this archive selection

## Overview

Early modern rationalists such as Descartes, Spinoza, and Leibniz built metaphysical systems from clear and distinct ideas or necessary truths. The label is comparative: few thinkers deny experience entirely, but they deny that all knowledge reduces to sensory impressions.

## Historical notes

Seventeenth-century continental rationalism responds to skepticism and scientific change; later Idealism and analytic a priori debates continue related arguments.

## Core ideas

-   Some truths are knowable by reason independent of particular sensory episodes.
-   Mathematics and logic model secure knowledge.
-   Metaphysics can be systematic and demonstrative.
-   Clear and distinct ideas (or sufficient reason) guide inquiry.

## Thinkers in this archive

[René Descartes](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/rene-descartes) , [Baruch Spinoza](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/baruch-spinoza) , [Karl Popper](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/karl-popper) , [Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/gottfried-wilhelm-leibniz) , [Maimonides](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/maimonides) , [Saadia Gaon](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/saadia-gaon) , [Judah Halevi](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/judah-halevi)

## FAQ

### What is rationalism in philosophy?

It is the view that reason is a primary source of knowledge, often including a priori truths.

### Who are famous rationalists?

Descartes, Spinoza, and Leibniz are the classic early modern trio.

### Where are rationalism quotes?

## Stoicism Quotes | Marcus, Seneca & Epictetus

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/schools/stoicism

School

# Stoicism quotes

Stoicism is a Hellenistic school teaching that living in agreement with nature and reason—through virtue—is the path to a flourishing life.

35 passages · 4 voices in this archive selection

## Overview

Founded by Zeno of Citium in Athens around 300 BCE, Stoicism divides philosophy into physics, logic, and ethics. Virtue is the only true good; externals such as wealth, health, and reputation are preferred or dispreferred indifferents. Passions are understood as mistaken judgments; the sage’s ideal is rational consistency, while progressors practice daily discipline.

## Historical notes

Early Stoics (Zeno, Cleanthes, Chrysippus) built a systematic school; Roman writers—Seneca, Epictetus, and Marcus Aurelius—preserve the most complete surviving ethical works. Modern readers often meet Stoicism as practical counsel, but classical Stoicism also included logic and a providential physics.

## Core ideas

-   Virtue is necessary and sufficient for happiness.
-   Some things are up to us (judgment, impulse); others are not.
-   Live according to nature—human nature as rational and social.
-   Practice: examine impressions before assenting to them.

## Thinkers in this archive

[Epictetus](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/epictetus) , [Seneca](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/seneca) , [Marcus Aurelius](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/marcus-aurelius) , [Cicero](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/cicero)

## FAQ

### What is Stoicism in simple terms?

Stoicism teaches that a good life centers on virtue and wise judgment, not on controlling external events.

### Who are the main Stoic philosophers?

Early founders include Zeno and Chrysippus; the most-read Roman Stoics are Seneca, Epictetus, and Marcus Aurelius.

## Seneca the Younger on Philosophy | Philosophy Defined

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/seneca-the-younger-philosophy-quotes

A thinker's position

# Seneca the Younger on Philosophy

Seneca wrote about how to live rather than how to know, and he wrote it in a form that survives: letters, meant to be read at intervals.

Philosophy Defined · Last reviewed 2026-10-05 · [How guides are written](https://www.philosophydef.com/editorial-policy)

On this page

1.  [Letters: a philosophy written to be re-read](#section-1)
2.  [Fear, and the arithmetic of the worst case](#section-2)
3.  [The natural questions: from the person to the cosmos](#section-3)
4.  [Practical ethics and the problem of wealth](#section-4)
5.  [FAQ](#faq)
6.  [Further reading](#further-reading)

## Short answer

Seneca the Younger's philosophy is Stoic ethics turned towards circumstance: the fixed duties of the school Stoics are kept intact, and the work is in applying them to fear, poverty, loss, and death. His letters ask what a person is actually afraid of and then subtract the fear from its object; they treat time as the only possession that cannot be seized; and they insist that consolation and argument are the same work. The natural questions extend the method from the individual to the cosmos, asking whether the heavens are material and whether the mind is a particle of fire.

## Letters: a philosophy written to be re-read

The letters to Lucilius are the form and the method at once. Seneca addresses one reader in the second person, does not pretend the letter concludes the subject, and revisits the same problems — fear, wealth, friendship, death — as circumstances change. A letter about dying when you are busy is not a meditation on death; it is a correction of a false estimate about what will still matter in an hour.

"All else belongs to others; time alone is ours" is the sentence the archive records with its Latin, \*tempus est unum quod suum est\*, because the popular versions translate it as a claim about a limited resource rather than about a category that is not subject to anyone else. That difference carries the whole argument: the objection to hoarding money or praise is not that they are worthless, it is that they never were yours to keep.

## Fear, and the arithmetic of the worst case

"There are more things that frighten us than crush us, and we suffer more of the imagination than the reality" is Seneca's most quoted line and his most systematically argued. The \*Natural Questions\* and the letters share a procedure: name what is feared, list what it actually does, and then count the difference between the two. He is not claiming fear is foolish in general; he is claiming the fear is usually larger than the thing.

"It is not because things are difficult that we do not dare; it is because we do not dare that they are difficult" is the same argument about action rather than feeling, and the archive notes that the compressed English and the standard translations differ slightly in the order of the clauses. The sense is that the perceived difficulty is frequently the difficulty of starting, and that starting is what the difficulty is borrowed from.

## The natural questions: from the person to the cosmos

The \*Natural Questions\* asks whether the stars are fires, whether the earth floats in air, whether the mind is a slender flame, and whether the sea is made of many waters. These are not exercises in scepticism for their own sake; each question is a way of asking whether the world is governed by reason, and the answers are graded rather than binary. Seneca accepts what can be demonstrated, concedes what is beyond demonstration, and locates the difference between the two.

"There is no easy way from the earth to the stars" is the line that names the difficulty properly. It is not a claim that effort is pointless; it is a claim that the mind cannot be transported upward and must climb, which is why the effort is real and why the ascent is available to anyone. The metaphor also keeps the argument honest about the difference between a person and a place.

## Practical ethics and the problem of wealth

Seneca is the Stoic who has to answer the charge against his own life, having spent a fortune and been adviser to a court. His position is not that possessions are irrelevant but that the person who makes his peace with having them does not become a different person on losing them. The letters on poverty and on power are written by someone who is unusually qualified to be suspected of hypocrisy, and they are where his ethics is least abstract.

"Leisure without study is death — a tomb for a living man" is the compressed form of a line he used of a mind with nothing to occupy it. Read alongside the letters on time, it makes a consistent claim: the danger is not stress but the absence of anything that requires a judgement. That is closer to what the letters do than to a rule about scheduling, and it is the reason Seneca's method has outlived the circumstances of his century.

## Frequently asked questions

### Who was Seneca the Younger?

Lucius Annaeus Seneca (c. 4 BCE – 65 CE), Stoic philosopher, dramatist, and adviser to the emperor Nero. The Younger distinguishes him from Seneca the Elder, his father and a rhetorician.

### What is Seneca's philosophy?

Stoic ethics applied to circumstance: fixed duties kept in full, and the work done in applying them to fear, poverty, loss, and death. His letters are the medium, and the natural questions extend the method to the physical world.

### What did Seneca say about time?

'All else belongs to others; time alone is ours' — tempus est unum quod suum est, in a letter to Lucilius. The point is not that time is short but that it is the one category not subject to anyone else's control.

## Further reading

-   Seneca, Letters to Lucilius
-   Seneca, Natural Questions (Naturales Quaestiones)
-   Seneca, On the Shortness of Life

## Philosophy Quotes About Action: Thinkers, Sources & Context

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/action

Theme

# Philosophy quotes about action

Action concerns agency: what it is to do something intentionally, and how thought becomes practice.

30 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

## Why this theme matters

Philosophy of action asks how intentions, reasons, habits, and consequences hang together. Ethical traditions often insist that knowing the good is incomplete without doing it.

## In the history of philosophy

Aristotelian praxis, Confucian unity of knowledge and action, Stoic exercises, and modern theories of intentionality all contribute to this theme.

## Thinkers in this collection

[Aristotle](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/aristotle) , [Seneca](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/seneca) , [Voltaire](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/voltaire) , [Hannah Arendt](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/hannah-arendt) , [William James](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/william-james) , [Auguste Comte](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/auguste-comte) , [Xunzi](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/xunzi) , [Laozi](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/laozi)

## Frequently asked questions

### What is action in philosophy?

An action is typically a deed done for a reason, as opposed to a mere bodily event or accident.

### Why do philosophers connect action and ethics?

Because moral evaluation usually concerns what agents do, intend, and could have done otherwise.

### Which traditions emphasize practice over theory?

Stoicism, Confucianism, pragmatism, and many Buddhist schools treat practice as the test of understanding.

# Philosophy quotes about affirmation

## Why this theme matters

## In the history of philosophy

Discussions of affirmation travel through Indian, Japanese and European modern traditions. Compare the quotations below with their school labels rather than forcing a single definition.

### What did philosophers say about affirmation?

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/choice

Theme

# Philosophy quotes about choice

Choice is the hinge of agency: selecting among options under reasons, constraints, and uncertainty.

15 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

## Why this theme matters

Free will, decision theory, and existential choice all ask how choosing is possible and what makes a choice one’s own.

## In the history of philosophy

Aristotelian prohairesis, Stoic assent, existential commitment, and modern behavioral science offer overlapping vocabularies.

## Thinkers in this collection

[Aristotle](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/aristotle) , [Friedrich Nietzsche](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/friedrich-nietzsche) , [Søren Kierkegaard](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/soren-kierkegaard) , [Jean-Paul Sartre](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/jean-paul-sartre) , [Hannah Arendt](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/hannah-arendt) , [William James](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/william-james) , [Dante Alighieri](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/dante-alighieri) , [Confucius](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/confucius)

## Frequently asked questions

### What is choice in philosophy?

It is the act of selecting among alternatives, often tied to responsibility and practical reason.

Compatibilists, libertarians, and determinists disagree; many still affirm practical responsibility.

## Philosophy Quotes About Courage: Thinkers, Sources & Context

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/courage

Theme

# Philosophy quotes about courage

Courage is the virtue of facing fear without abandoning judgment—central to ethics from Aristotle to modern existential resolve.

14 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

## Why this theme matters

Philosophers ask whether courage is fearlessness or right action amid fear, and how it relates to recklessness, endurance, and moral courage in public life.

## In the history of philosophy

Greek andreia, Confucian and martial ethics, Stoic endurance, and civil-disobedience traditions all refine the concept.

## Thinkers in this collection

[Socrates](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/socrates) , [Seneca](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/seneca) , [Immanuel Kant](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/immanuel-kant) , [Ralph Waldo Emerson](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/ralph-waldo-emerson) , [Bertrand Russell](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/bertrand-russell) , [Confucius](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/confucius) , [Paul Tillich](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/paul-tillich) , [Søren Kierkegaard](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/soren-kierkegaard)

## Frequently asked questions

### What is courage in philosophy?

Typically a mean between cowardice and rashness: persevering for worthy ends despite fear.

### Is moral courage different from physical courage?

Many ethicists distinguish facing bodily danger from risking status, career, or approval for a principle.

### Where are philosophy quotes about courage?

This theme gathers English passages on bravery, fear, and steadfastness.

## Philosophy Quotes About Death | Stoic & Epicurean

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/death

Theme

# Philosophy quotes about death

Philosophy quotes about death confront mortality, fear, legacy, and what a finite life can mean.

9 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

## Why this theme matters

Some argue that death is nothing to us; others that mortality intensifies value; still others that grief and remembrance are ethical tasks. The theme sits between metaphysics and consolation.

## In the history of philosophy

Epicurean therapy, Stoic rehearsals of mortality, Platonic immortality debates, and Buddhist attention to impermanence remain touchstones.

## Thinkers in this collection

[Epicurus](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/epicurus) , [Seneca](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/seneca) , [Marcus Aurelius](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/marcus-aurelius) , [Lucretius](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/lucretius) , [Michel de Montaigne](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/michel-de-montaigne) , [Plato](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/plato) , [Baruch Spinoza](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/baruch-spinoza) , [Gabriel Marcel](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/gabriel-marcel)

## Frequently asked questions

### What do philosophers say about death?

They ask whether death harms the one who dies, how fear of death should be handled, and what duties the living owe the dead.

### Is fear of death irrational?

Some schools say yes if death is non-existence; others treat fear as informative about attachment and unfinished responsibility.

### Where can I find philosophy quotes about death?

This theme gathers English passages from Stoic, Epicurean, Chinese, and modern sources.

1.  > Death is nothing to us: for what has been dissolved has no sensation, and what has no sensation is nothing to us.

3.  > Do not act as if you were going to live ten thousand years. Death hangs over you. While you live, while it is in your power, be good.

    De Rerum Natura III.830

6.  > Depart then in peace; the one who releases you is also at peace.

## Philosophy Quotes About Desire: Thinkers, Sources & Context

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/desire

Theme

# Philosophy quotes about desire

Desire drives action and suffering alike; philosophy asks which desires to educate, restrain, or affirm.

17 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

## Why this theme matters

Ethics and moral psychology analyze appetite, love, ambition, and addiction. Stoic, Buddhist, and psychoanalytic traditions treat desire as trainable rather than merely given.

## In the history of philosophy

From Plato’s tripartite soul to Spinoza’s conatus and modern consumer critique, desire remains a hinge between metaphysics and ethics.

## Thinkers in this collection

[Epictetus](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/epictetus) , [Epicurus](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/epicurus) , [Boethius](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/boethius) , [The Book of Changes](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/the-book-of-changes) , [David Hume](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/david-hume) , [Lucretius](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/lucretius) , [Thomas Hobbes](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/thomas-hobbes) , [Jean-Paul Sartre](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/jean-paul-sartre)

## Frequently asked questions

### What is desire in philosophy?

It is a directed wanting that can motivate action—evaluated as natural, distorted, or educable depending on the school.

### Should we eliminate desire?

Some ascetic ideals aim at quieting craving; others seek ordered or enlightened desire rather than elimination.

## Philosophy Quotes About Dignity: Thinkers, Sources & Context

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/dignity

Theme

# Philosophy quotes about dignity

Dignity names the worth that persons claim simply as persons—and the respect that worth demands.

18 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

## Why this theme matters

Kantian and rights-based ethics make dignity central; other traditions speak of face, honor, or Buddha-nature. Politics asks how institutions honor or violate dignity.

## In the history of philosophy

From Stoic cosmopolitanism and Confucian respect to modern human rights, dignity bridges ethics and law.

## Thinkers in this collection

[Blaise Pascal](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/blaise-pascal) , [Immanuel Kant](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/immanuel-kant) , [John Stuart Mill](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/john-stuart-mill) , [Albert Camus](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/albert-camus) , [Seneca](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/seneca) , [Mencius](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/mencius) , [Mary Wollstonecraft](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/mary-wollstonecraft) , [Qian Mu](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/qian-mu)

## Frequently asked questions

### What is dignity in philosophy?

It is the intrinsic or status-based worth of persons that grounds respect and limits on treatment.

### Is dignity the same as honor?

Honor is often social and hierarchical; dignity is frequently claimed as equal and inalienable—though histories intertwine.

## Philosophy Quotes About Experience: Thinkers, Sources & Context

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/experience

Theme

# Philosophy quotes about experience

Experience is the lived encounter with world and self—foundation or limit for knowledge, art, and ethics.

23 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

## Why this theme matters

Empiricists treat experience as the source of ideas; phenomenologists describe its structure; pragmatists treat it as experimental and revisable.

## In the history of philosophy

From Aristotelian aisthesis to Locke, Hume, Dewey, and phenomenology, experience is a battleground for epistemology and metaphysics.

## Thinkers in this collection

[John Locke](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/john-locke) , [George Berkeley](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/george-berkeley) , [David Hume](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/david-hume) , [William James](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/william-james) , [John Dewey](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/john-dewey) , [Alfred North Whitehead](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/alfred-north-whitehead) , [Nishida Kitaro](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/nishida-kitaro) , [Al-Ghazali](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/al-ghazali)

## Frequently asked questions

### What is experience in philosophy?

It is the first-person undergoing of sensations, thoughts, and situations—interpreted differently across schools.

### Is all knowledge from experience?

Empiricists lean yes; rationalists and others defend a priori elements or innate structures.

### Where are philosophy quotes about experience?

This page gathers English passages on perception, habit, and lived life.

1.  > Whence has it all the materials of reason and knowledge? To this I answer, in one word, from experience.
    
    [John Locke: “Whence has it all the materials of reason…”](https://www.philosophydef.com/quotes/q0186)  
    An Essay Concerning Human Understanding, II.i.2
    
2.  > Their being is to be perceived.
    
    [George Berkeley: “Their being is to be perceived.”](https://www.philosophydef.com/quotes/q0187)  
    A Treatise Concerning the Principles of Human Knowledge, §3
    
3.  > For my part, when I enter most intimately into what I call myself, I always stumble on some particular perception or other.
    
    [David Hume: “For my part, when I enter most intimately…”](https://www.philosophydef.com/quotes/q0250)  
    Treatise I.4.6
    
4.  > Consciousness…does not appear to itself chopped up in bits…It is nothing jointed; it flows.

## Philosophy Quotes About Freedom: Thinkers, Sources & Context

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/freedom

Theme

# Philosophy quotes about freedom

Freedom is among the most searched and most contested themes in philosophy: what it is to choose, to be responsible, and to live without illegitimate constraint.

55 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

## Why this theme matters

Philosophers distinguish several ideas under the single word freedom. Negative freedom emphasizes non-interference; positive freedom emphasizes the capacity to act according to reasons, virtue, or authentic desire. Stoic writers often relocate freedom inside judgment; modern political philosophers ask which institutions protect or destroy it.

## In the history of philosophy

From Stoic accounts of the will to Confucian debates about ritual and spontaneity, from Rousseau and Kant to twentieth-century liberalism and existentialism, freedom has been treated as both a metaphysical and a civic problem. The archive gathers English passages that keep these tensions visible rather than resolving them in advance.

## Thinkers in this collection

[Plato](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/plato) , [Epictetus](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/epictetus) , [Seneca](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/seneca) , [Marcus Aurelius](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/marcus-aurelius) , [Michel de Montaigne](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/michel-de-montaigne) , [Baruch Spinoza](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/baruch-spinoza) , [Jean-Jacques Rousseau](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/jean-jacques-rousseau) , [Søren Kierkegaard](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/soren-kierkegaard)

## Frequently asked questions

### What did philosophers say about freedom?

They disagreed. Some treat freedom as absence of external constraint; others as reasoned self-rule; still others as a lived stance toward fortune, desire, or political power.

### What is the philosophical definition of freedom?

There is no single definition. A useful starting point is the ability to act according to one’s own deliberation without domination—then ask what counts as one’s own, and what counts as domination.

### What are the best philosophy quotes about freedom?

The strongest passages usually clarify a distinction: freedom versus license, freedom versus fate, or civic liberty versus inner independence. Browse the quotations below for verified English renderings.

## Philosophy Quotes About Happiness: Thinkers, Sources & Context

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/happiness

Theme

# Philosophy quotes about happiness

Happiness—or flourishing—is a central aim in ethics: what makes a life go well, and whether pleasure alone is enough.

21 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

## Why this theme matters

Greek eudaimonia, Buddhist analyses of craving, utilitarian happiness, and modern well-being research all contest the meaning of a good life.

## In the history of philosophy

Aristotle, Epicurus, the Stoics, and Confucian flourishing ideals remain primary references; later utilitarianism reframed happiness as aggregable preference or pleasure.

## Thinkers in this collection

[Aristotle](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/aristotle) , [Epicurus](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/epicurus) , [John Stuart Mill](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/john-stuart-mill) , [Albert Camus](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/albert-camus) , [Bertrand Russell](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/bertrand-russell) , [Jeremy Bentham](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/jeremy-bentham) , [Plato](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/plato) , [Thomas Hobbes](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/thomas-hobbes)

## Frequently asked questions

### What is happiness in philosophy?

It may mean pleasure, desire satisfaction, or eudaimonic flourishing through virtue and meaningful activity.

### Is happiness the same as pleasure?

Not for most virtue ethicists; pleasure can be part of a good life without exhausting it.

## Philosophy Quotes About Humanity: Thinkers, Sources & Context

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/humanity

Theme

# Philosophy quotes about humanity

Humanity names both the species and the moral quality of being humane—bridging anthropology and ethics.

26 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

## Why this theme matters

Philosophers ask what makes humans distinctive, what we owe one another as humans, and how “humanity” can include or exclude.

## In the history of philosophy

Confucian ren, Renaissance humanism, Enlightenment rights, and critiques of humanism from various directions keep the theme contested.

## Thinkers in this collection

[Immanuel Kant](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/immanuel-kant) , [Seneca](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/seneca) , [Albert Camus](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/albert-camus) , [Jean-Paul Sartre](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/jean-paul-sartre) , [The Doctrine of the Mean](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/the-doctrine-of-the-mean) , [Protagoras](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/protagoras) , [Blaise Pascal](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/blaise-pascal) , [John Locke](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/john-locke)

## Frequently asked questions

### What is humanity in philosophy?

It can mean the human species, shared capacities, or the virtue of humane regard for others.

### Is human nature fixed?

Debates range from fixed essences to historical and cultural formation of human possibilities.

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/humility

Theme

# Philosophy quotes about humility

Humility appears in this archive as a live philosophical concern—not a slogan. These verified English passages show how thinkers treat humility as a problem of judgment, practice, or explanation.

12 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

## Why this theme matters

Across 4 recurring voices here (notably Confucius and Kwame Anthony Appiah), humility is framed through Stoicism and Confucianism. Some passages define humility; others warn how it fails; still others relocate it inside habit, community, or language.

## In the history of philosophy

Discussions of humility travel through Greek, Chinese and Africana traditions. Compare the quotations below with their school labels rather than forcing a single definition.

## Philosophy Quotes About Inquiry: Thinkers, Sources & Context

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/inquiry

Theme

# Philosophy quotes about inquiry

Inquiry is the disciplined pursuit of better questions and answers—philosophy as method rather than dogma.

17 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

## Why this theme matters

Socratic elenchus, scientific method, and pragmatist experimentalism treat inquiry as self-correcting. The ethics of inquiry asks for intellectual honesty.

## In the history of philosophy

Academies, laboratories, and public debate inherit ideals of inquiry that philosophy both practices and criticizes.

## Thinkers in this collection

[Aristotle](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/aristotle) , [Heraclitus](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/heraclitus) , [Anselm of Canterbury](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/anselm-of-canterbury) , [Michel de Montaigne](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/michel-de-montaigne) , [Plutarch](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/plutarch) , [Confucius](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/confucius) , [The Doctrine of the Mean](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/the-doctrine-of-the-mean) , [Francis Bacon](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/francis-bacon)

## Frequently asked questions

### What is inquiry in philosophy?

It is the process of investigating questions with reasons, evidence, and willingness to revise belief.

### How does philosophical inquiry differ from science?

It often targets conceptual and normative questions science presupposes, while remaining continuous with scientific curiosity.

### Where are philosophy quotes about inquiry?

## Philosophy Quotes About Justice: Thinkers, Sources & Context

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/justice

Theme

# Philosophy quotes about justice

Justice concerns fairness, rights, desert, and the arrangement of institutions that claim to treat people as equals.

19 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

## Why this theme matters

Distributive, retributive, and restorative justice name different problems. Political philosophy asks what a just society owes its members and outsiders.

## In the history of philosophy

Plato’s Republic, Confucian rightful rule, social-contract theories, and contemporary egalitarian debates structure the field.

## Thinkers in this collection

[Socrates](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/socrates) , [Plato](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/plato) , [Mencius](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/mencius) , [John Locke](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/john-locke) , [Wang Yangming](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/wang-yangming) , [Epicurus](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/epicurus) , [Simone de Beauvoir](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/simone-de-beauvoir) , [Elizabeth Anscombe](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/elizabeth-anscombe)

## Frequently asked questions

### What is justice in philosophy?

It is the virtue and institutional standard of giving each their due—though “due” is endlessly debated.

### What are the types of justice?

Common distinctions include distributive, procedural, retributive, and restorative justice.

## Philosophy Quotes About Knowledge | Epistemology in the Archive

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/knowledge

Theme

# Philosophy quotes about knowledge

Knowledge is the philosophical study of what we can justifiably claim to know—and where certainty ends.

74 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

## Why this theme matters

Epistemology asks whether knowledge is justified true belief, reliable tracking of the world, or something else; it also asks how perception, testimony, memory, and reason contribute.

## In the history of philosophy

From Plato’s dialogues and Indian pramāṇa theory to Descartes, Hume, Kant, and contemporary analytic epistemology, the theme remains a core branch of philosophy.

## Thinkers in this collection

[Socrates](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/socrates) , [Augustine of Hippo](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/augustine-of-hippo) , [Michel de Montaigne](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/michel-de-montaigne) , [René Descartes](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/rene-descartes) , [Arthur Schopenhauer](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/arthur-schopenhauer) , [William James](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/william-james) , [Auguste Comte](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/auguste-comte) , [Albert Camus](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/albert-camus)

## Frequently asked questions

### What is knowledge in philosophy?

A leading starting point is justified true belief, refined by debates about Gettier cases, reliability, evidence, and understanding.

### How do philosophers distinguish knowledge from opinion?

By asking for reasons, methods, and standards of evidence that can survive scrutiny—not by intensity of conviction alone.

### Where can I read philosophy quotes about knowledge?

## Philosophy Quotes About Language: Thinkers, Sources & Context

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/language

Theme

# Philosophy quotes about language

Language appears in this archive as a live philosophical concern—not a slogan. These verified English passages show how thinkers treat language as a problem of judgment, practice, or explanation.

22 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

## Why this theme matters

Across 4 recurring voices here (notably Ludwig Wittgenstein and Kwasi Wiredu), language is framed through Analytic Philosophy and Africana Philosophy. Some passages define language; others warn how it fails; still others relocate it inside habit, community, or language.

## In the history of philosophy

Discussions of language travel through Africana and European modern traditions. Compare the quotations below with their school labels rather than forcing a single definition.

## Thinkers in this collection

[Ludwig Wittgenstein](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/ludwig-wittgenstein) , [John Stuart Mill](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/john-stuart-mill) , [Voltaire](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/voltaire) , [Epictetus](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/epictetus) , [Elizabeth Anscombe](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/elizabeth-anscombe) , [Sophie Oluwole](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/sophie-oluwole) , [Audre Lorde](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/audre-lorde) , [Averroes](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/averroes)

## Frequently asked questions

### What did philosophers say about language?

They disagreed in productive ways. In this archive, Ludwig Wittgenstein, Kwasi Wiredu, and related voices treat language as something to clarify, cultivate, or critique—not merely to celebrate.

### Where can I find philosophy quotes about language?

This theme page gathers 15 verified English quotations tagged Language, with links to thinkers and sources.

### How should I read quotes about language?

Read the sentence, then check school and source. A compact line is an entry point into an argument about language, not a substitute for the surrounding text.

## Philosophy Quotes About Learning: Thinkers, Sources & Context

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/learning

Theme

# Philosophy quotes about learning

Learning is philosophy’s practical twin: how judgment is formed through study, error, dialogue, and habit.

14 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

## Why this theme matters

Education is not only information transfer; it is the shaping of attention and character. Confucian learning, Socratic midwifery, and Deweyan growth offer rival models.

## In the history of philosophy

Academies, monasteries, universities, and modern schooling all encode philosophies of learning—often silently.

## Thinkers in this collection

[Seneca](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/seneca) , [Confucius](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/confucius) , [Zengzi](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/zengzi) , [Xunzi](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/xunzi) , [The Doctrine of the Mean](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/the-doctrine-of-the-mean) , [Zhu Xi](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/zhu-xi) , [Wang Guowei](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/wang-guowei) , [Michel de Montaigne](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/michel-de-montaigne)

## Frequently asked questions

### What do philosophers say about learning?

They treat learning as cultivation of reason and character, not merely accumulation of facts.

### Who emphasizes learning most?

Confucius, Plato, Dewey, and many Stoic teachers make education central to the good life.

### Where are philosophy quotes about learning?

Browse this theme and the philosophy of education guide.

## Philosophy Quotes About Life | Meaning, Virtue & How to Live

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/life

Theme

# Philosophy quotes about life

Philosophy quotes about life ask what makes a life good, meaningful, or worth examining—questions that drive ethics, religion, and everyday decision.

37 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

## Why this theme matters

Life is both a biological fact and a practical project. Philosophers debate flourishing, suffering, mortality, and the standards by which a biography can be judged successful or wasted.

## In the history of philosophy

Eudaimonia in Greek ethics, Daoist naturalness, Buddhist attention to suffering, existential authenticity, and contemporary meaning-of-life debates all appear across this theme.

## Thinkers in this collection

[Socrates](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/socrates) , [Epicurus](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/epicurus) , [Seneca](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/seneca) , [Baruch Spinoza](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/baruch-spinoza) , [Henry David Thoreau](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/henry-david-thoreau) , [John Dewey](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/john-dewey) , [Albert Camus](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/albert-camus) , [William James](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/william-james)

## Frequently asked questions

### What is the meaning of life in philosophy?

Answers range from flourishing and virtue to service, creativity, love, or the claim that meaning is constructed rather than discovered.

### Why do people search for philosophy quotes about life?

Because compact sentences can reopen a large question quickly—especially when they come from traditions that have tested the question for centuries.

### Which thinkers wrote most about how to live?

Aristotle, the Stoics, Confucius, Epicurus, and many modern existential writers make the art of living central rather than peripheral.

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/love

Theme

# Philosophy quotes about love

Love in philosophy ranges from friendship and desire to care, justice, and the transformation of the self.

28 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

## Why this theme matters

Greek distinctions among eros, philia, and agape, Confucian relational ethics, and modern debates about romantic love keep the theme philosophically precise rather than merely sentimental.

## In the history of philosophy

Plato’s Symposium, Aristotle on friendship, Augustine on ordered loves, and contemporary ethics of care all leave traces in these quotations.

## Thinkers in this collection

[Plato](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/plato) , [Aristotle](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/aristotle) , [Seneca](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/seneca) , [Augustine of Hippo](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/augustine-of-hippo) , [Arthur Schopenhauer](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/arthur-schopenhauer) , [Mencius](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/mencius) , [Mozi](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/mozi) , [Simone Weil](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/simone-weil)

## Frequently asked questions

### What is love according to philosophy?

It can be desire, mutual goodwill, recognition, attachment, or a commitment to another’s good—often several of these at once.

### Did ancient philosophers value friendship more than romance?

Many Greek and Roman texts give friendship a central ethical role; later European traditions elevate romantic love in different ways.

## Philosophy Quotes About Mind: Thinkers, Sources & Context

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/mind

Theme

# Philosophy quotes about mind

Philosophy of mind asks what consciousness, thought, and mental life are—and how they relate to body and world.

20 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

## Why this theme matters

Dualism, materialism, functionalism, and phenomenological descriptions compete. AI renews old questions about understanding and experience.

## In the history of philosophy

From Aristotle’s psyche and Buddhist analyses of mind to Descartes, Wittgenstein, and cognitive science, the theme spans metaphysics and epistemology.

## Thinkers in this collection

[Arthur Schopenhauer](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/arthur-schopenhauer) , [Bertrand Russell](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/bertrand-russell) , [Dhammapada](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/dhammapada) , [Diamond Sutra](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/diamond-sutra) , [Wang Yangming](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/wang-yangming) , [Boethius](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/boethius) , [Baruch Spinoza](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/baruch-spinoza) , [John Locke](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/john-locke)

## Frequently asked questions

### What is the mind in philosophy?

It names the locus of thought, feeling, and consciousness—whether as soul, brain process, or patterned activity.

### Can machines have minds?

That depends on what mind requires: behavior, information processing, or subjective experience. The debate remains open.

## Philosophy Quotes About Morality: Thinkers, Sources & Context

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/morality

Theme

# Philosophy quotes about morality

Morality in philosophy concerns right and wrong, obligation, and the standards by which we judge persons and acts.

34 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

## Why this theme matters

Moral philosophy asks whether morality is objective, how reasons bind us, and how character, rules, and consequences relate. Traditions differ on whether duty, virtue, or outcomes come first.

## In the history of philosophy

From Confucian and Greek virtue vocabularies to Kantian duty, utilitarianism, and critiques of moral ideology, the theme remains central to public life.

## Thinkers in this collection

[Socrates](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/socrates) , [Plato](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/plato) , [Immanuel Kant](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/immanuel-kant) , [Arthur Schopenhauer](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/arthur-schopenhauer) , [The Great Learning](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/the-great-learning) , [Iris Murdoch](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/iris-murdoch) , [Bhagavad Gita](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/bhagavad-gita) , [Baruch Spinoza](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/baruch-spinoza)

## Frequently asked questions

### What is morality in philosophy?

It is the domain of norms about right action, good character, and what we owe one another—studied systematically in ethics.

### How is morality different from ethics?

In everyday speech they overlap; academically, ethics often names the philosophical study of moral practices and concepts.

## Philosophy Quotes About Nature: Thinkers, Sources & Context

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/nature

Theme

# Philosophy quotes about nature

Philosophy quotes about nature ask what the cosmos is, how humans belong in it, and whether “natural” can guide ethics or politics.

41 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

## Why this theme matters

Nature may mean physical cosmos, living world, human nature, or a normative standard of what ought to be. Presocratics, Daoists, Stoics, and modern environmental thinkers share the word while disagreeing about its force.

## In the history of philosophy

From Greek physis and Chinese ziran to Rousseau’s state of nature and contemporary ecology, the theme links metaphysics, ethics, and politics.

## Thinkers in this collection

[Heraclitus](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/heraclitus) , [Lucretius](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/lucretius) , [Baruch Spinoza](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/baruch-spinoza) , [Thomas Hobbes](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/thomas-hobbes) , [Immanuel Kant](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/immanuel-kant) , [Arthur Schopenhauer](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/arthur-schopenhauer) , [Henry David Thoreau](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/henry-david-thoreau) , [Ludwig Wittgenstein](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/ludwig-wittgenstein)

## Frequently asked questions

### What do philosophers mean by nature?

They may mean the physical world, human dispositions, or a standard of right order—contexts decide which sense is in play.

### Is living according to nature a Stoic idea?

Yes. Stoicism treats living in agreement with nature—as rational and social—as the ethical end, though “nature” is richly defined.

## Philosophy Quotes About Order: Thinkers, Sources & Context

Source: https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/order

Theme

# Philosophy quotes about order

Order names cosmos, ritual, law, and the patterned stability that makes shared life possible—or oppressive.

20 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

## Why this theme matters

Philosophers ask whether order is discovered in nature, imposed by rulers, or cultivated through custom. Chaos and creativity stand as its counterparts.

## In the history of philosophy

Cosmological order, Confucian ritual order, and modern bureaucratic order show how the same word travels across metaphysics and politics.

## Thinkers in this collection

[Plato](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/plato) , [Heraclitus](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/heraclitus) , [Thomas Hobbes](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/thomas-hobbes) , [Alfred North Whitehead](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/alfred-north-whitehead) , [Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/gottfried-wilhelm-leibniz) , [Ralph Waldo Emerson](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/ralph-waldo-emerson) , [The Great Learning](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/the-great-learning) , [The Doctrine of the Mean](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/the-doctrine-of-the-mean)

## Frequently asked questions

### What is order in philosophy?

It can mean natural regularity, social arrangement, or moral harmony—context decides which sense is meant.

### Is order always desirable?

Not if it encodes injustice; critical philosophies ask whose order and at what cost.

### Where are philosophy quotes about order?

This theme collects passages on harmony, law, measure, and structure.

## Why this theme matters

Across 4 recurring voices here (notably Frantz Fanon and Kwame Anthony Appiah), otherness is framed through Africana Philosophy and Platonic Moral Philosophy. Some passages define otherness; others warn how it fails; still others relocate it inside habit, community, or language.
